documents.title: Syllabus Requirements and Guidelines (AI Policies section)
documents.summary: Official undergraduate integrity office page with three adaptable syllabus statements (permit, prohibit, designated assignments), drafting considerations, and Honor Code reporting duties. The decision on AI use is left to each instructor.
documents.stance_why: The page gives instructors three template statements running 'from permitting to prohibiting' generative AI and says a tailored statement per class is better. The university sets no stance itself and hands the decision to instructors with a tier list; the fixed rules are only the Honor Code pledge and reporting duty.

units.why: The office 'encourages all faculty to state a clear policy on student use of generative AI for each class syllabus'; a recommendation to instructors to put an AI statement in each syllabus, so P09 with modality should.
units.anchor: encourages all faculty to state a clear policy on student use of generative AI for

units.why: The three statements run 'from permitting to prohibiting the use of generative AI in class'; the university offers a menu of named options instead of one rule, so P05 (tiers). P04 fits less well because the point is the sorted menu.
units.anchor: three possible policy statements, from permitting to prohibiting the use of generative AI in class

units.why: The page says 'It is better for each class to have a statement tailored to its specific requirements'; the AI rule is left to each class, so P04. The tier menu (P05) is coded separately.
units.anchor: better for each class to have a statement tailored to its specific requirements

units.why: Template 1 says 'use of generative AI tools is permitted for all assignments' provided it contributes to learning; a permit-by-default course rule with a condition, so P02.
units.anchor: use of generative AI tools is permitted for all assignments
units.policy: Template 1: generative AI tools are permitted for all assignments if the student uses them to contribute to learning of the course content, not to replace original work.

units.why: In the same sentence AI is allowed 'but not to replace original work', which bars AI from producing the student's work; P19 is the nearest type, although the template frames it as the condition of a permit.
units.anchor: but not to replace original work
units.policy: AI must not replace the student's original work.
units.fit_note: Framed as a condition on an otherwise permitted use rather than as a ban.

units.why: Template 1 says 'You must properly acknowledge when and how AI tools have been used in your submissions'; disclosure with each submission, P24.
units.anchor: You must properly acknowledge when and how AI tools have been used in your submissions

units.why: The template says 'Failure to disclose AI use or submitting AI-generated work as entirely your own without critical engagement will constitute a violation of the Honor Code'; nondisclosure is itself the violation, so P28.
units.anchor: Failure to disclose AI use or submitting AI-generated work as entirely your own without critical

units.why: The template's 'it is your responsibility to ask your faculty member before proceeding' tells students who are unsure to ask first, P10. The sentence repeats in all three templates; coded once.
units.anchor: If you are ever uncertain about the use of AI, it is your responsibility to

units.why: Template 2 states 'the use of any generative AI tools is strictly prohibited for all graded assignments, exams, and assessments', a default ban on graded work, P01.
units.anchor: use of any generative AI tools is strictly prohibited for all graded assignments, exams, and

units.why: 'All work must represent your own independent effort and original thinking' requires submitted work to be the student's own, P29.
units.anchor: All work must represent your own independent effort and original thinking

units.why: Template 2 says AI used 'to draft, edit, summarize, or generate content is considered unauthorized assistance and a violation of the Honor Code'; it classes use as misconduct (P36) and also covers editing and summarizing.
units.anchor: use of AI tools to draft, edit, summarize, or generate content is considered unauthorized assistance

units.why: 'Violations will be reported and handled in accordance with Virginia Tech's Honor Code procedures' points to the formal procedure for misuse, P81.
units.anchor: Violations will be reported and handled in accordance with Virginia Tech’s Honor Code procedures

units.why: Template 3 says AI 'may only be used for specific assignments that are designated by the instructor'; allowed only where designated, so P107 (limited to designated cases) rather than P04, since the default outside is a ban.
units.anchor: generative AI tools may only be used for specific assignments that are designated by the

units.why: 'Any assignment requiring use of AI will be clearly outlined in the assignment instructions' ties the expectation to assignment instructions; it also lists 'brainstorming, analyzing information or editing' as example tasks. P09 for the communication duty.
units.anchor: Any assignment requiring use of AI will be clearly outlined in the assignment instructions

units.why: 'For all other assignments, the use of AI tools is prohibited and constitutes unauthorized assistance' fixes a fallback ban outside designated assignments, P06.
units.anchor: For all other assignments, the use of AI tools is prohibited and constitutes unauthorized assistance

units.why: 'students must disclose how AI was used through appropriate citations' is a disclosure rule, P24.
units.anchor: students must disclose how AI was used through appropriate citations

units.why: The pledge 'is to be written out on all graded assignments at the university and signed by the student'; a signed integrity pledge, P111.

units.why: 'All Undergraduate course syllabi shall contain a section that states and refers the student to the Honor Code Procedures' requires a syllabus integrity section; not AI-specific, but the university's required syllabus element, P09.

units.fit_note: Requires an Honor Code section in every syllabus, not an AI statement specifically.

units.why: 'A student who has doubts ... is responsible for obtaining specific guidance from the course instructor before submitting' tells students unsure of a use to ask, P10.

units.anchor: Students are strongly discouraged from misusing unauthorized online sources including generative artificial intelligence outlets

units.anchor: Ignorance of the rules does not exclude any member of the University community

units.anchor: Any suspected violation of the Honor Code should be reported promptly, in writing

units.anchor: OUAI requires human analysis of any work being reported as AI plagiarism, although AI detector

documents.summary: Teaching-center guidance for faculty on deciding AI policy: understand the tools, follow the university framework and Honor Code, be careful with detectors, set and explain clear expectations, and consider redesigning assessment. It leaves the student-use rule to instructors.
documents.stance_why: The page is guidance to instructors: it says appropriate uses 'vary from course to course' and tells faculty to 'establish carefully considered course policies'. It sets no university-wide rule on student use, so the decision is delegated to instructors.

documents.title: Responsible and Ethical AI Framework for Virginia Tech (v1.0 Sep 2025)
documents.summary: The July 2025 AI Working Group report (v1.0) proposes seven principles, a three-tier risk framework, an AI Working Committee, policy revisions (Honor Code, IP, research misconduct), AI literacy and tool recommendations. Teaching and learning is one domain; much is governance, research and operations.
documents.stance_why: The framework is an institution-wide governance document that sets principles, a risk-tier scheme and a plan for later guides and policy revisions, and states that 'No formal AI policies currently exist'. It sets no stance on student AI use and leaves it to later guidance and instructors, so delegates.

units.why: The report says the group was 'charged with developing a framework for responsible AI use across the university's administrative, teaching, outreach, and research operations'; it states purpose and scope of the institution-wide framework, P56.
units.anchor: framework for responsible AI use across the university’s administrative, teaching, outreach, and research operations

units.why: 'Virginia Tech's governance infrastructure lacks formal AI policies' and 'No formal AI policies currently exist' admit there is no AI-specific policy, P108.
units.anchor: No formal AI policies currently exist, making governance establishment the top priority

units.why: The group 'recommends establishing a permanent AI Working Committee as part of IT governance'; names the body that will own AI policy, P80.
units.anchor: recommends establishing a permanent AI Working Committee as part of IT governance

units.why: The committee 'maintains authority over AI-specific policies, risk assessment, and implementation guidance'; who owns and interprets the policy, P80.
units.anchor: AI Working Committee maintains authority over
units.policy: The AI Working Committee maintains authority over AI-specific policies, risk assessment, and implementation guidance.

units.why: Specific authority for policy development 'will be determined through the IT governance reform process'; decision rights are still open, noted under P80 with a fit note.
units.anchor: Specific authority for AI policy development and approval will be determined through the IT governance
units.fit_note: States that decision authority is not yet fixed, rather than naming an owner.

units.why: Recommends 'Revise Five Critical Policies' including the Undergraduate Honor Code (Policy 6000) for AI gaps; a commitment to revise policy, P54.
units.anchor: Undertake immediate formal review of five foundational institutional policies, including the Undergraduate Honor Code

units.why: The Honor Code review should set 'precise definitions of appropriate usage, attribution requirements ... and detection and adjudication procedures for AI-related misconduct'; the Honor Code is to be revised for AI, P54.
units.anchor: establish clear standards for AI-assisted academic work
units.fit_note: Names the content the Honor Code revision should add: appropriate usage, attribution, detection and adjudication.

units.why: Research policies need 'supporting citation standards for large language model usage' and 'disclosure requirements'; a planned research-disclosure rule, P62.
units.anchor: supporting citation standards for large language model usage

units.why: The IP policy needs 'clarification of ownership frameworks for AI-generated works'; ownership of AI outputs, P52.
units.anchor: clarification of ownership frameworks for AI-generated works

units.why: The Visual Media Policy 'must be reviewed to consider the growing challenges of AI-generated imagery and deepfake technology'; the deepfake concern under P75 (AI-enabled threats), with a fit note since it is a policy review.
units.anchor: The Visual Media Policy (Policy 8205) must be reviewed to consider the growing challenges
units.policy: The Visual Media Policy (Policy 8205) must be reviewed to consider the growing challenges of AI-generated imagery and deepfake technology.
units.fit_note: A commitment to review a policy for deepfakes, not guidance to users on spotting threats.

units.why: Security policies need 'guidelines for AI-enhanced surveillance systems' that 'balance security effectiveness with privacy protection'; operational AI governance, P76.
units.anchor: Safety and Security Policies (e.g. Policiy 5617) would benefit from guidelines
units.policy: Safety and Security Policies (e.g. Policy 5617) would benefit from guidelines for AI-enhanced surveillance systems.

units.why: Three 'practical implementation guides' will give 'syllabus language templates that establish clear expectations for AI use disclosure'; the institution will supply sample syllabus language, P110.
units.anchor: syllabus language templates that establish clear expectations for AI use disclosure

units.why: The guide 'includes assessment adaptation strategies that account for AI tool availability while preserving educational rigor'; assessment redesign around AI, P35.
units.anchor: assessment adaptation strategies that account for AI tool availability while preserving educational rigor

units.why: The Teaching and Learning subgroup 'establishes student AI literacy curriculum alongside faculty and staff training programs'; AI literacy for students and staff, P70.
units.anchor: establishes student AI literacy curriculum alongside faculty and staff training programs

units.why: 'foundational AI literacy modules designed for universal deployment across all students, faculty, and staff'; community-wide AI literacy training, P70.
units.anchor: foundational AI literacy modules designed for universal deployment across all students, faculty, and staff

units.why: 'specialized faculty training modules that develop pedagogical expertise in AI integration' supports faculty learning, P63.
units.anchor: specialized faculty training modules that develop pedagogical expertise in AI integration

units.why: The Principles 'apply to all students, faculty, and staff, contractors, and affiliated partners who design, procure, or use AI'; the scope of the framework, P61.
units.anchor: principles apply to all students, faculty, and staff, contractors, and affiliated partners who design, procure,
units.fit_note: Sets who is covered rather than defining AI.

units.why: Principle 1: 'We use AI only in ways that further Virginia Tech's teaching, research, and outreach mission'; a general principle in the institution-wide framework, P56.
units.anchor: We use AI only in ways that further Virginia Tech’s teaching, research, and outreach mission

units.why: Principle 2: 'We explore new AI tools boldly while weighing benefits against risks' encourages exploring AI and weighing benefits against risks, P118.
units.anchor: We explore new AI tools boldly while weighing benefits against risks
units.fit_note: Also encourages bold exploration, not only weighing.

units.why: Principle 3: 'AI should extend—not replace—human insight, creativity, and well-being'; AI must not replace human thinking, P32.
units.anchor: AI should extend—not replace—human insight, creativity, and well-being
units.fit_note: Stated for all AI use at the university, not specifically for student work.

units.why: Principle 4: 'We consider environmental impact, intellectual property rights, and social consequences before deploying AI'; names harms and environmental costs, P53.
units.anchor: We consider environmental impact, intellectual property rights, and social consequences before deploying AI

units.why: Principle 5: 'We disclose AI use to those affected by it' is a disclosure principle; P103 (tell people when they are dealing with AI) fits, though it is stated as the institution's own duty.
units.anchor: We disclose AI use to those affected by it
units.fit_note: Covers disclosure of AI use to those affected generally, not only interaction with an AI system.

units.why: 'strive to reduce bias' and 'explainable' systems; bias and fairness concern, P53.
units.anchor: design, procure, and use AI systems that are explainable and strive to reduce bias

units.why: Principle 6: 'People remain accountable for decisions influenced by AI. A human should always be in the loop for important decisions' keeps humans responsible for decisions about people, P73.
units.anchor: A human should always be in the loop for important decisions

units.why: 'Individuals using AI systems are responsible for adhering to existing university policies, standards, and security review processes'; comply with existing policy, P77.
units.anchor: Individuals using AI systems are responsible for adhering to existing university policies, standards, and security

units.why: 'will provide AI-related upskilling, reskilling, and educational opportunities' commits to AI training, P70.
units.anchor: will provide AI-related upskilling, reskilling, and educational opportunities

units.why: Principle 7: 'We safeguard personal and institutional data used in AI systems and interactions' protects personal data, P50.
units.anchor: We safeguard personal and institutional data used in AI systems and interactions

units.why: 'obtain consent from individuals who interact with AI' where appropriate; P103 is the nearest type (people's right to know they deal with AI), though consent goes beyond notice.
units.anchor: where appropriate, obtain consent from individuals who interact with AI
units.fit_note: Asks for consent from people who interact with AI, beyond telling them.

units.why: The principles are 'living guidance that will evolve through practice' with 'Regular review cycles'; a revisit commitment, P54.
units.anchor: Regular review cycles will ensure they continue to serve Virginia Tech’s mission

units.why: The three-tier framework: low-risk 'basic productivity tools, general writing assistance, simple data analysis' need 'self-certification', medium-risk 'educational applications' need 'departmental approval', high-risk need committee review; named tiers, P05, and tool review, P65. P05 chosen as the sorting scheme is the main content.
units.anchor: Medium Risk Applications: Advanced analytical tools, decision support systems, educational applications.
units.policy: The framework sorts AI applications into low, medium and high risk tiers, with oversight matched to risk: self-certification for low, departmental approval for medium, and AI Working Committee review for high.
units.fit_note: Tiers classify AI applications by risk for oversight, not levels of student AI use.

units.why: 'High Risk Applications: AI systems affecting personnel decisions, student outcomes, or resource allocation' require committee review; human review of consequential decisions, P73.
units.anchor: AI systems affecting personnel decisions, student outcomes, or resource allocation
units.fit_note: Requires committee review of such systems rather than a human decision on each case.

units.why: The group will form 'integrated subgroups' for Teaching and Learning, Research and Operations; AI for research outputs, publication standards and data handling, P62.
units.anchor: establishes publication standards and data handling protocols for AI-assisted research

units.why: The Operations subgroup 'develops guidelines for automated decision systems with appropriate human oversight requirements' and 'establishes vendor evaluation procedures'; operational AI and vendor review, P76.
units.anchor: develops guidelines for automated decision systems with appropriate human oversight requirements

units.why: The Copilot approval was given 'after demonstrating secure integration with the university's existing M365 tenant'; institutional approval of a tool, P65.
units.anchor: Microsoft Copilot Suite was given approval for campus use after demonstrating secure integration

units.why: ChatGPT Edu 'has not been officially selected as an enterprise platform for Virginia Tech'; states which tools are sanctioned, P92.
units.anchor: has not been officially selected as an enterprise platform for Virginia Tech

units.why: Rolai, 'an AI-tutoring add-on now under evaluation in selected Canvas courses', is a course-level AI tutor tool, P17.
units.anchor: an AI-tutoring add-on now under evaluation in selected Canvas courses

units.why: 'establishing ongoing evaluation processes for emerging AI technologies and tools' is recurring institutional review of tools, P65.
units.anchor: establishing ongoing evaluation processes for emerging AI technologies and tools

units.why: 'The institution is committed to proactively addressing potential barriers including cost constraints' and a digital divide; equitable access, P51.
units.anchor: prioritizes ensuring that all advancements bridge rather than exacerbate existing digital divides

units.why: AI tool evaluation criteria 'explicitly incorporate rigorous accessibility standards' for assistive technologies; accessibility of AI tools, P97.
units.anchor: AI tool evaluation criteria explicitly incorporate rigorous accessibility standards

units.why: 'The university will implement alternative access methods for core functions where necessary'; an alternative-access plan, P97.
units.anchor: The university will implement alternative access methods for core functions where necessary

units.why: 'The university conducts regular algorithmic auditing processes that systematically evaluate AI systems for bias'; auditing deployed systems, P98.
units.anchor: The university conducts regular algorithmic auditing processes that systematically evaluate AI systems for bias

units.why: 'Transparency requirements for AI decision-making processes, particularly in high-impact applications' say people should understand how AI influences decisions; P103 is the nearest type.
units.anchor: Transparency requirements for AI decision-making processes, particularly in high-impact applications affecting student success
units.fit_note: About transparency of AI-influenced decisions rather than telling people they face an AI.

units.why: 'All AI applications must adhere to ethical data use protocols and applicable data transfer compliance requirements'; comply with law and policy, P77.
units.anchor: All AI applications must adhere to ethical data use protocols and applicable data transfer compliance

units.why: 'quarterly forums, annual assessment surveys' and community listening sessions engage the community on AI, P88.
units.anchor: Continuous stakeholder engagement through quarterly forums, annual assessment surveys
units.fit_note: Engagement is with internal stakeholders as much as the public.

units.why: 'regular review cycles for the foundational guidance' and 'quarterly updates' to the guides: the policy will be revisited, P54.
units.anchor: establishing regular review cycles for the foundational guidance and associated standards

units.why: 'consistent benchmarking against peer institutions' is peer engagement on AI, P88.
units.anchor: consistent benchmarking against peer institutions will further inform adaptive strategies

units.why: Faculty 'identified critical gaps in current guidance regarding AI use in dissertations, theses, and examinations'; an acknowledged gap in guidance on research writing and exams, P62.
units.anchor: critical gaps in current guidance regarding AI use in dissertations, theses, and examinations
units.fit_note: Also names examinations, which P62 does not cover.

units.why: 'the unreliability of AI detection tools creates enforcement dilemmas'; detectors are unreliable, P39.
units.anchor: the unreliability of AI detection tools creates enforcement dilemmas

units.why: 'Faculty rightly note the environmental costs of AI systems' and concerns about how submitted data may be used; names environmental cost and data concerns, P53.
units.anchor: Faculty rightly note the environmental costs of AI systems

units.why: The annual assessment should evaluate 'impacts on academic integrity, pedagogical values, and environmental sustainability'; evidence on how AI affects learning, P55.
units.anchor: evaluate not just technical effectiveness but also impacts on academic integrity, pedagogical values, and environmental
units.fit_note: Evidence is on integrity, pedagogy and the environment, not directly on learning outcomes.

units.why: The teaching and research groups 'should prioritize developing nuanced guidance for high-stakes academic assessments'; a commitment to produce assessment guidance, P35.
units.anchor: should prioritize developing nuanced guidance for high-stakes academic assessments
units.fit_note: Commits to producing guidance on assessment, not to a specific redesign.

units.why: 'foster external partnerships with industry leaders, government agencies, and peer institutions' is engagement with peers and partners, P88.
units.anchor: foster external partnerships with industry leaders, government agencies, and peer institutions

units.why: The AI frontier theme 'AI for Intelligence Augmentation' reflects the philosophy that 'AI should enhance rather than replace human capabilities'; P32 for the stance on human thinking.
units.anchor: AI should enhance rather than replace human capabilities
units.fit_note: Institutional research philosophy, not a rule for student work.

units.why: Teaching and learning: 'Guidelines emphasize human oversight, fact-checking, and disclosing AI use in coursework'; verification and disclosure expectations, P31.
units.anchor: Guidelines emphasize human oversight
units.policy: Guidelines emphasize human oversight, fact-checking, and disclosing AI use in coursework.
units.fit_note: Also names disclosure of AI use in coursework (P24).

units.why: 'Faculty are encouraged to update syllabi to clarify expectations regarding AI tool use' is the syllabus-statement recommendation, P09.
units.anchor: Faculty are encouraged to update syllabi to clarify expectations regarding AI tool use

units.why: 'The university encourages both faculty and students to experiment with AI tools to explore their potential in learning, teaching, and daily tasks' is a default encouraging AI use, P02.
units.anchor: The university encourages both faculty and students to experiment with AI tools

units.why: 'strict guidelines against using AI tools with sensitive, confidential, or regulated data'; protect confidential data, P50.
units.anchor: strict guidelines against using AI tools with sensitive, confidential, or regulated data

units.why: 'limited formal agreements with most external AI tool providers, meaning standard university security and privacy protections may not apply' warns of risk with unlicensed tools, P114.
units.anchor: limited formal agreements with most external AI tool providers, meaning standard university security and privacy
units.fit_note: Stated as an institutional challenge; does not assign liability to users.

units.why: The Honor Code needs 'Need clear definitions of acceptable AI use in assignments' and 'Attribution requirements for AI-generated content'; concrete gap list, P54.
units.anchor: Need clear definitions of acceptable AI use in assignments
units.fit_note: Gap list for the Honor Code revision.

units.why: 'Faculty evaluation: May need AI use disclosure considerations'; an item on instructor AI disclosure for review, P47.
units.anchor: Faculty evaluation: May need AI use disclosure considerations
units.fit_note: A flagged item for future review, not a rule.

units.why: HR: 'Bias prevention in AI-assisted hiring processes' and 'Human oversight standards for AI-assisted HR functions'; human oversight of employment decisions, P73.
units.anchor: Human oversight standards for AI-assisted HR functions
units.fit_note: Listed as an area needing guidance, not a rule.

units.why: IT policy: 'Incident Response: AI-related security incident procedures' flags a needed reporting and response procedure, P71.
units.anchor: Incident Response: AI-related security incident procedures
units.fit_note: Listed as an area to be addressed, not a rule.

units.why: 'AI Responsible Use guidelines' to be integrated into acceptable use policies; links AI to existing policy, P77.
units.anchor: integration of AI Responsible Use guidelines into existing acceptable use policies
units.fit_note: A plan to bring AI into existing policies, not a rule on users.

units.why: The pilot found 'Accuracy and Hallucination Concerns (31% of responses): Need for fact-checking and verification'; evidence of the need to verify output, P31.
units.anchor: Accuracy and Hallucination Concerns (31% of responses): Need for fact-checking and verification

units.why: 'Dependency and Skill Attrition Concerns (6% of responses): Risk of over-reliance on AI tools' records concern that AI use erodes skill, P41.
units.anchor: Dependency and Skill Attrition Concerns (6% of responses): Risk of over-reliance on AI tools
units.fit_note: Survey finding from employees in a pilot, not a student-learning claim.

units.why: Pilot participants rated 94% of respondents reporting 'increased productivity' and 95% 'improved work quality'; evidence on AI effects on work, P55.
units.anchor: 94% of respondents reported increased productivity
units.fit_note: Evidence on staff and faculty productivity, not student learning.

units.why: 'Mandatory 30-minute training provided foundation' in the pilot; required AI training, P70.
units.anchor: Mandatory 30-minute training provided foundation
units.fit_note: Describes a pilot's training for employees.

units.why: The Copilot pilot 'Accessibility testing is ongoing; until Excel analytics ships with full keyboard and screen-reader support, units relying heavily on data analysis should weigh Copilot's benefits against that gap'; accessibility of a tool, P97.
units.anchor: until Excel analytics ships with full keyboard and screen-reader support

documents.title: Artificial Intelligence (AI) at Virginia Tech (College of Engineering)
documents.date_or_term: undated; page notes later university AI governance
documents.summary: A short College of Engineering IT page with ten guidelines for safe use of AI (security, data, verification, disclosure), example admin and research uses, and notes on teaching: instructors set rules, detectors are unreliable. The page itself points to ai.vt.edu as more current.
documents.stance_why: The page lists general guidelines (verify output, protect sensitive data, document usage) and says 'Instructors should establish guidelines for student use of AI'. It sets no college rule on student AI use and hands it to instructors, so delegates.

units.why: The page says it 'provides guidelines and resources for safely integrating AI into academic and administrative practices at the VT College of Engineering'; the college-level scope, P56.
units.anchor: guidelines and resources for safely integrating AI into academic and administrative practices

units.why: 'Understand security concerns when using AI tools.' is a security-awareness rule, P50 (protect data and use vetted tools is the nearest type).
units.anchor: Understand security concerns when using AI tools.
units.fit_note: General security awareness, no specific data rule.

units.why: 'Explore and experiment with AI cautiously' permits experimentation with care, P02.
units.anchor: Explore and experiment with AI cautiously.

units.why: 'Never input sensitive data, such as Personally Identifiable Information (PII), or information protected by the Family Educational Rights and Privacy Act (FERPA)' protects personal data, P50.
units.anchor: such as Personally Identifiable Information (PII)
units.policy: Never input sensitive data, such as Personally Identifiable Information (PII), or information protected by the Family Educational Rights and Privacy Act (FERPA).

units.why: 'Review AI output against reliable sources to assure accuracy. Verify sources.' tells users to verify AI output, P31.
units.anchor: Review AI output against reliable sources to assure accuracy. Verify sources.

units.why: 'Consult your departmental IT staff before installing AI tools or plug-ins on university owned computers' requires approval before installing AI tools on university machines, P107 (prior approval).
units.anchor: Consult your departmental IT staff before installing AI tools or plug-ins on university owned computers.
units.fit_note: Consult-before-install, not a strict approval requirement.

units.why: 'Stay informed about AI advancements.' is a duty to keep up with AI developments, P102.
units.anchor: Stay informed about AI advancements.

units.why: 'Promote ethical AI use, including respecting intellectual property and avoiding plagiarism. Model this behavior for students in your own work.' asks for ethical use and for instructors to model it, P112.
units.anchor: Model this behavior for students in your own work.
units.policy: Promote ethical AI use, including respecting intellectual property and avoiding plagiarism. Model this behavior for students in your own work.
units.fit_note: Also asks for ethical use, IP respect and avoiding plagiarism generally.

units.why: 'Document usage of AI tools for transparency and accountability.' is a general documentation duty, P24 (nearest disclosure rule).
units.anchor: Document usage of AI tools for transparency and accountability.
units.fit_note: Asks to document use for transparency, with no named recipient or submission.

units.why: 'Review Policies to address legal compliance and ethical standards.' links to existing laws and policies, P77.
units.anchor: Review Policies to address legal compliance and ethical standards.

units.why: The administrative use list names 'Drafting email correspondence' and 'Meeting transcription and summarization' among uses of AI in operations; operational AI use, P76.
units.anchor: Drafting email correspondence
units.policy: Administrative uses of AI named include scheduling and calendar management, drafting email correspondence, customer support chatbots, data filtering and organization, website code creation, meeting transcription and summarization, and video and audio editing.
units.fit_note: A list of example uses rather than a rule.

units.why: The research use list names 'Summarize research and generate bibliographies to assist with literature reviews'; AI for literature work, P104.
units.anchor: Summarize research and generate bibliographies to assist with literature reviews
units.fit_note: Listed as a use case with no condition to verify sources.

units.why: The research list also names 'Analyze large datasets from experiments, identifying patters and generating visualizations'; data analysis, P89.
units.anchor: Analyze large datasets from experiments, identifying patters and generating visualizations

units.why: The research list also names 'Assist in drafting and refining research proposals' and editing collaborative documentation; writing support, P91.
units.anchor: Assist in drafting and refining research proposals, making it easier to secure funding.

units.why: 'Instructors should establish guidelines for student use of AI, and ensure honor code compliance.' leaves rules to instructors, P04.
units.anchor: Instructors should establish guidelines for student use of AI, and ensure honor code compliance.

units.why: 'AI detection tools can produce false positives, complicating enforcement.' says detectors are unreliable, P39.
units.anchor: AI detection tools can produce false positives, complicating enforcement.

units.why: 'Students have access to the same detection software, allowing them to easily disguise AI.' notes that detection can be evaded, P82.
units.anchor: Students have access to the same detection software, allowing them to easily disguise AI.

units.why: 'Since this page was created, the University has taken great strides in AI governance. Please visit ai.vt.edu for the most up to date information.' defers to newer guidance, P115 (point to further guidance).
units.anchor: Please visit ai.vt.edu for the most up to date information.
units.fit_note: Also admits the page is out of date.

notes: No computing-unit or course documents were collected for Virginia Tech (searched: computing none-found, course deferred). The OUAI page (vt-1) offers three template statements as tiers; the TLOS page (vt-2) and framework (vt-3) are guidance and governance documents. The framework is long; units were coded for teaching, learning, integrity, governance, tool review, privacy, accessibility and policy-review commitments. Appendix content (readiness scores, pilot costs) was coded only where it states a policy-relevant fact. Items in the framework that are plans ('would benefit from', 'will') are coded with modality informs or should, not as rules.
